# Validation results (generated by tests/validate.py)

## 1. Independent re-implementation, all 11,200 tickets

Mismatches: {'breach': 0, 'created_shift': 0, 'cause': 0, 'resolver_shift': 0}. Tickets in independent path: 11,200 (pipeline: 11,200).

This proves the code does what the rules say. It does NOT prove the rules are right (both are mine); see 2.

## 2. Hold-out: does 'no cover at creation' explain breaches out of sample?

Rule learned on 2025-Q3 only (predict breach when channel+cause breached >50% in train). Scored on 7,093 tickets, 2025-Q4 to 2026-Q2.

- accuracy 88.0%, precision 78.3%, recall 71.1%

- confusion: TP 1244, FP 345, FN 506, TN 4998

- breaches the rule cannot explain (FN): 506 of 1750 = 28.9%. These are ordinary in-shift breaches (~9% floor) and the half of overnight EMAIL tickets that breach.

- overnight email is the weak spot: 628 tickets, 49% breach - the rule predicts 'no breach' so it misses those breaches, and the exact hour decides (8h target vs 06:00 start).

- placebo: before 2025-07-01 gap tickets = 2 (both are 30 Jun night); breach rate 9.3%. In-shift breach rate by quarter is flat: 2025Q1 9.7%, 2025Q2 8.9%, 2025Q3 10.0%, 2025Q4 9.2%, 2026Q1 9.2%, 2026Q2 9.2%.

## 3. What the naive report would have said

- No dedupe: 11,816 rows vs 11,200 real tickets; breaches counted 2,555 vs 2,440.

- Treating UTC as IST puts 68% of tickets in the wrong shift.

- Charging breaches to the resolver's shift (helpdesk default), Jul 2025-Jun 2026: {'Day': 323, 'Morning': 1906}. Of Morning's, 1529 were created overnight with nobody rostered.

- Agent view: 33 agents carry breaches from the coverage gap in their names.
